definition: containing a lot of moisture in the air; damp and often warm

collocations.example: Singapore has a hot and humid climate all year.
The humid air made our clothes feel damp.

definition: a feeling that something is true, based on instinct rather than facts

collocations.example: I have a hunch that she will arrive late.
The detective decided to play a hunch and wait.

definition: a period of silence, especially after noise or excitement

collocations.example: A sudden hush fell over the crowded room.
An expectant hush settled before the speaker began talking.

definition: the practice of keeping yourself and your surroundings clean to stay healthy

collocations.example: Good personal hygiene helps prevent the spread of disease.
Restaurants must follow strict food hygiene rules every day.

definition: a religious song that people sing together to praise God

collocations.example: The congregation stood up to sing a hymn.
The choir practiced a Christmas hymn for the service.

definition: intense advertising or publicity that exaggerates how good something is

collocations.example: The new phone received a lot of media hype.
Ignore the marketing hype and read honest customer reviews.

definition: based on an imagined situation rather than a real one

collocations.example: The interviewer asked me a purely hypothetical question.
Let's consider a hypothetical situation to test the plan.

definition: so emotional or excited that you cannot control your behavior

collocations.example: She became hysterical when she heard the terrible news.
A hysterical crowd pushed forward to see the star.

definition: a person who is greatly admired or loved by many people

collocations.example: Thousands of fans screamed for the young pop idol.
He became a teen idol after his first film.

definition: lacking knowledge or awareness about something

collocations.example: Many drivers are ignorant of the new parking rules.
Without reading, children may remain largely ignorant.

definition: morally wrong; not following accepted standards of good behavior

collocations.example: The company was punished for its immoral behavior.
Many people consider lying to customers deeply immoral.

definition: to formally charge a public official with serious misconduct in office

collocations.example: Congress voted to impeach the president for misconduct.
Lawmakers moved to impeach a judge accused of corruption.

definition: to slow down or make it difficult for something to happen or move

collocations.example: Poor communication can seriously impede progress on the project.
The fallen tree continued to impede traffic for hours.

definition: about to happen soon, especially something bad

collocations.example: Dark clouds gave a feeling of impending disaster.
A sense of impending doom filled the quiet room.

definition: something that encourages a process or activity to develop more quickly

collocations.example: The award gave a new impetus to her research.
The tax cuts should provide an impetus for economic growth.

definition: to make a person or place poor

collocations.example: Rising prices continue to impoverish many working families.
Heavy taxes can impoverish the economy over time.

definition: a mark left on a surface by pressing something onto it

collocations.example: Her boots left a clear imprint in the snow.
The war left an indelible imprint on the nation.

definition: not done on purpose; accidental

collocations.example: The report contained an inadvertent error in the totals.
Staff training helps prevent the inadvertent disclosure of data.

definition: to officially open a building, event, or service with a ceremony

collocations.example: The mayor arrived to inaugurate the new art exhibition.
The company will inaugurate a new ferry service tomorrow.

definition: having a human or physical form; in person

collocations.example: To his enemies, the dictator seemed the devil incarnate.
The villain in the film is evil incarnate.

definition: to destroy something completely by burning it

collocations.example: The plant was built to incinerate household waste safely.
The intense fire can completely incinerate the old documents.

definition: to cut carefully into a surface with a sharp instrument

collocations.example: The surgeon will incise the skin to reach the muscle.
The craftsman used a blade to carefully incise the pattern.

definition: including everything mentioned, such as costs or items, with nothing left out

collocations.example: The hotel rate is inclusive of breakfast and parking.
We booked an all-inclusive holiday to the Greek islands.

definition: impossible to understand

collocations.example: His handwriting was totally incomprehensible to the whole class.
The legal document was incomprehensible to ordinary readers.

definition: a small amount by which something increases, or one step in a series of increases

collocations.example: Employees receive an annual increment to their basic salary.
The temperature rose slowly in small increments all afternoon.

definition: to keep eggs warm until the young birds come out

collocations.example: The female bird will incubate the eggs for two weeks.
Farmers sometimes artificially incubate eggs in a warm machine.

definition: feeling or showing anger because something seems unfair or wrong

collocations.example: The workers were indignant at the sudden cut in pay.
She became indignant when nobody believed her honest account.

definition: so important or useful that you cannot manage without it

collocations.example: Her experience made her indispensable to the whole team.
Computers are now an indispensable part of office work.

definition: to formally admit someone into an organization or official position

collocations.example: They will induct the famous singer into the Hall of Fame.
The club held a ceremony to induct new members.

definition: soldiers who are trained to fight on foot

collocations.example: An entire infantry division was sent to the border.
The light infantry advanced quickly through the dense forest.

definition: to enter a place or group secretly, usually to get information or cause harm

collocations.example: Spies tried to infiltrate the organization over several years.
The soldiers managed to infiltrate enemy lines at night.

definition: the arrival of a large number of people or things at the same time

collocations.example: The festival brought a huge influx of tourists.
A sudden influx of refugees overwhelmed the small border town.

definition: providing useful information

collocations.example: The lecture was highly informative and easy to follow.
She gave an informative talk about healthy eating habits.

definition: to break a law or agreement, or to limit someone's rights

collocations.example: Copying the software would infringe copyright and break the law.
Critics say the new law may infringe civil liberties.

definition: an official order from a court telling someone to do or stop doing something

collocations.example: They obtained a court injunction to stop the building work.
The judge agreed to grant an injunction against the company.

definition: to write or carve words on a surface such as stone or metal

collocations.example: The jeweller will inscribe a name inside the ring.
They chose to inscribe a short message on the trophy.

definition: words that are written or carved on something, such as a monument or gift

collocations.example: The inscription on the gravestone had almost worn away.
The author added a personal inscription inside my book.

definition: a hormone produced by the body that controls the level of sugar in the blood

collocations.example: Being overweight can increase a person's insulin resistance.
People with diabetes often have to inject insulin daily.

definition: relating to people who use force to fight against their own government

collocations.example: Several insurgent groups controlled parts of the mountainous region.
An insurgent attack damaged the bridge near the capital.

definition: the ability to think, reason, and understand things clearly

collocations.example: The young lawyer was admired for her sharp intellect.
The puzzle was designed to test the human intellect.

definition: to exchange one thing for another, or swap two things

collocations.example: The two teams met to interchange ideas about design.
The two offices regularly interchange information about their customers.

definition: stopping and starting again at irregular times; not continuous

collocations.example: Intermittent rain spoiled our plans for the garden party.
The faulty switch caused the intermittent operation of the machine.

definition: a student or new graduate who works somewhere to gain practical experience

collocations.example: She worked as a marketing intern during the summer.
The company hired three summer interns this year.

definition: too bad, difficult, or unpleasant to bear or accept

collocations.example: The workers protested about the intolerable conditions in the factory.
The heat in the office became intolerable by noon.

definition: having many small parts or details arranged in a complicated way

collocations.example: The carpet was woven with an intricate pattern of flowers.
The artist painted the tiny insect in intricate detail.

definition: the act of entering a place or affecting a situation where you are not wanted

collocations.example: She saw the phone call as an unwanted intrusion.
Citizens complained about government intrusion into their private lives.

definition: the ability to understand or know something without conscious reasoning

collocations.example: Sometimes you should trust your intuition when making decisions.
In a flash of intuition, she solved the problem.

definition: based on feelings and instinct rather than careful thought or facts

collocations.example: A good nurse develops an intuitive sense for patients' needs.
Children often have an intuitive understanding of fairness.

definition: to turn something upside down or put it in the opposite order

collocations.example: Invert the bottle quickly to pour out the thick sauce.
The lens will invert the image of the candle.

definition: done without intention or conscious control

collocations.example: A loud noise can cause an involuntary movement of the hand.
Blinking is an involuntary reaction to bright light.

definition: to make clothes smooth by pressing them with a heated iron

collocations.example: He had to iron a shirt before the interview.
She likes to iron the clothes while watching television.

definition: so attractive or powerful that you cannot stop yourself wanting or doing it

collocations.example: She felt an irresistible urge to laugh during the meeting.
The cake looked so good that guests found it irresistible.

definition: to supply water to land or crops using pipes, channels, or sprinklers

collocations.example: Farmers use river water to irrigate the fields.
Without rain, they must irrigate crops throughout the summer.

definition: becoming annoyed or impatient very easily

collocations.example: He tends to become irritable when he is tired.
The long delay made the passengers increasingly irritable.

definition: an island, especially a small one or one used in a name

collocations.example: They spent their holiday on the Isle of Wight.
The monks lived alone on a remote isle.

definition: an uncomfortable feeling on the skin that makes you want to scratch it

collocations.example: He reached behind to scratch an itch on his back.
The wool sweater gave her a persistent itch.

definition: a large wild cat with yellow fur and black spots, found in the Americas

collocations.example: The photographer hoped to film a wild jaguar in the jungle.
Tourists were thrilled to spot a jaguar near the river.

definition: an unhappy feeling of anger or resentment because someone has something you want

collocations.example: In a fit of jealousy, he deleted her photos.
Her promotion caused some professional jealousy among her colleagues.

definition: a small, strong vehicle that can travel over rough ground

collocations.example: The soldiers arrived in an army jeep covered with mud.
They loaded the supplies into the back of a jeep.

definition: a soft, sweet food made from fruit juice and sugar, often spread on bread

collocations.example: The child asked for a peanut butter and jelly sandwich.
She spread strawberry jelly thickly on her warm toast.

definition: a shirt worn by a member of a sports team, often with a number on it

collocations.example: He proudly wore his favorite team's football jersey.
Every player received a new team jersey before the match.

definition: happy and cheerful

collocations.example: The guests were in a jolly mood all evening.
Our neighbor is a jolly fellow who loves telling jokes.

definition: a sudden violent movement or shock

collocations.example: The train stopped with a jolt that woke everyone.
A sudden jolt threw the passengers forward in their seats.

definition: a container with a handle and a lip, used for pouring liquids

collocations.example: She filled the milk jug and placed it on the table.
The waiter brought a jug of water to our table.

definition: to manage several activities or responsibilities at the same time

collocations.example: Many parents struggle to juggle work and family life.
A good manager can juggle multiple tasks without stress.

definition: a member of a jury in a court of law

collocations.example: An alternate juror replaced the one who fell ill.
The judge asked each juror to consider the evidence carefully.

definition: in a fair and reasonable way; with good reason

collocations.example: A good leader must always act justly toward every employee.
Every employee deserves to be treated justly at work.

definition: a container with a lid and handle, used for boiling water

collocations.example: She switched on the electric kettle to make tea.
Please put the kettle on; our guests will arrive soon.

definition: saying something as a joke rather than meaning it seriously

collocations.example: Don't worry, I was just kidding about the extra homework.
Are you kidding me, or did we really win?

definition: a light frame covered with paper or cloth that is flown in the wind on a string

collocations.example: The children went to the park to fly a kite.
He made a colorful paper kite for his younger brother.

definition: a round handle or control button on a door, drawer, or machine

collocations.example: The door knob was loose and fell off completely.
Turn the control knob to adjust the oven temperature.

definition: one of the joints where your fingers bend or join your hand

collocations.example: He has an annoying habit of cracking his knuckles.
After the fall, she nursed a bruised knuckle for days.

definition: a lamp with a transparent case that protects the flame or light inside

collocations.example: Rows of red paper lanterns lit up the street.
The guide carried a lantern through the dark cave.

definition: a small metal fastening for a door, gate, or window

collocations.example: He lifted the latch and pushed the gate open.
She left the door on the latch for her son.

definition: present but not yet active, developed, or visible

collocations.example: A good teacher can bring out a child's latent talent.
The survey revealed strong latent demand for the new service.

definition: the distance of a place north or south of the equator, measured in degrees

collocations.example: The map clearly showed the lines of latitude and longitude.
Winters are long and dark at such a high latitude.

definition: hot liquid rock that flows from a volcano

collocations.example: Rivers of molten lava poured down the mountainside.
The village lay directly in the path of the lava flow.

definition: a plant with purple flowers and a sweet smell, often used in perfume

collocations.example: A few drops of lavender oil can help you relax.
We drove past a beautiful field of lavender in France.

definition: a narrow flat surface that sticks out from a wall or cliff

collocations.example: She placed a pot of herbs on the window ledge.
The climber rested on a narrow ledge halfway up.

definition: a vegetable with large green leaves, usually eaten raw in salads

collocations.example: The salad was made with crisp iceberg lettuce.
She bought a head of lettuce at the market.

definition: to officially demand and collect a tax or other payment

collocations.example: The government decided to levy a tax on sugary drinks.
The city may levy a charge on overnight visitors.

definition: a plant with large, showy, often white or colored flowers

collocations.example: A single water lily floated on the still pond.
She carried a bouquet of white lilies down the aisle.

definition: a large, comfortable, expensive car, often driven by a professional driver

collocations.example: The couple arrived at the party in a stretch limousine.
A chauffeured limousine waited outside the hotel entrance.

definition: the series of family members from whom a person or animal is descended

collocations.example: The family can trace its lineage back five centuries.
She was proud of her ancient and noble lineage.

definition: a large ship that carries passengers on long journeys

collocations.example: They crossed the Atlantic on a luxury ocean liner.
The huge cruise liner docked at the busy port.

definition: to close a business and sell its assets in order to pay its debts

collocations.example: The directors voted to liquidate the failing company.
They had to liquidate their assets to repay the loan.

definition: a unit for measuring the volume of liquids in the metric system

collocations.example: You should drink about a liter of water daily.
The price of fuel rose by five cents per liter.

definition: a fixed set of words and actions used in a religious ceremony

collocations.example: The priest celebrated the divine liturgy early on Sunday morning.
The minister read the liturgy slowly from the old book.

definition: a small reptile with a long body, four legs, and a long tail

collocations.example: A small wall lizard darted across the warm stones.
A basking lizard lay motionless in the afternoon sun.

definition: bread that has been baked in one piece and can be sliced

collocations.example: He bought a fresh loaf of bread from the bakery.
She cut thick slices from the crusty loaf.

definition: to hate someone or something very much

collocations.example: The two rivals clearly loathe each other intensely.
I absolutely loathe getting up early on cold mornings.

definition: a sea animal with a hard shell, two large claws, and eight legs, eaten as food

collocations.example: The restaurant is famous for its grilled lobster.
He cracked open the large lobster claw with a tool.

definition: a particular area or neighborhood

collocations.example: There are few good schools in the locality.
The factory provides jobs for the surrounding locality.

definition: a small cupboard that can be locked, used for storing personal belongings

collocations.example: He kept his sports kit in a gym locker.
The players gathered in the locker room before the game.

definition: a railway engine that pulls a train

collocations.example: The museum displays an old steam locomotive from the 1920s.
A powerful diesel locomotive pulled the long freight train.

definition: the central place where something happens or is concentrated

collocations.example: Parliament remained the true locus of power in the nation.
The market square was the locus of activity in town.

definition: a room or space just below the roof of a house, often used for storage

collocations.example: They paid for a loft conversion to add a bedroom.
We store our old suitcases in the loft.
